text:
incident-bot: [P1] automatic page - multiple serving nodes flapped in eu-west-1; autoscaler oscillation detected, error patterns: CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED / OOM, container restarts. Pager: oncall-alex @oncall page (3478901234)

oncall-alex: seeing ~30% request 5xxs for dedicated-hosted pool, dashboards show rapid scale up then immediate node evictions. customers potentially affected: real-time chat, low latency tiers. pushing to triage.

sre-maya: confirmed. k8s events show repeated CrashLoopBackOff on pod set `redwood-runtime-eu-serve-*`, node kubelet logs show `eviction` + `gpus: driver lost` around 3478901200-3478901300.

infra-li: i'm on infra. early hypothesis: autoscaler reacted to short-lived load spike, scaled to new GPU nodes that failed driver init (nvml) causing serial evictions, autoscaler keeps launching to meet target -> thrash.

runtime-jon: adding logs snippet from one crash: ```
E0321 14:07:12.345678 1 runtime.cc:412] CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED: kernel launch failed
I0321 14:07:12.345700 1 model_runner.cc:88] kv_cache corrupted, clearing cache for session 0x7ff
W0321 14:07:12.346000 1 container_manager.cc:210] container restart (exit_code=137)
```

support-sarah: started triage DM with customer success for top 3 customers on low-latency plan. CS @cs-tom, can you confirm any direct reports of errors?

cs-tom: customer RM says two customers in EU reported lag and dropped responses starting ~14:06. no widespread billing/ingestion errors, but app fallback to queued mode triggered. flagged as P1.

oncall-alex: action plan: 1) pause autoscaler for eu-west-1 (to stop oscillation), 2) cordon new nodes that fail nvml, 3) scale down to stable baseline, 4) collect driver logs and triage root cause. assigning tasks.

infra-li: pausing autoscaler now: `kubectl -n redwood patch hpa runtime-autoscaler -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":4,"maxReplicas":6}}'` -> done (min 4 max 6).

runtime-jon: cordoning suspicious nodes: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=eu-gpu -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl cordon` -> cordoned 3 nodes that show nvml errors. Also setting taint `gpu-init-failed=true:NoSchedule`.

sre-maya: restarted one container with instrumentation, captured driver stack: `nvidia-smi` intermittent communication error, then kernel OOPS in one host. suspect kernel-module mismatch after AMI patch. collecting host boot logs and kernel versions.

infra-li: checking AMI rollouts: there was an automated infra image update yesterday for eu-west that included NVIDIA driver 535.x -> some hosts show 525.x leftover modules. mismatch leads to nvml failing on init. rolling back image is in flight.

eng-prod: if AMI is to blame we need a controlled rollback. recommend we prevent any new nodes with updated AMI from joining pool until confirmed. we can set scheduler constraint or bump a label to prevent autoscaler from using new launch template.

oncall-alex: agreed. @infra-li set launch template to previous working AMI id and disable new node provisioning in autoscaler until rollback completes. also notify deployments to pause any infra-image CI jobs.

infra-li: done - launch template reverted to ami-0a7b2c3d (previous). autoscaler templates updated. CI infra image pipeline paused.

support-sarah: customer comms: sending a short note to impacted customers explaining transient degraded latency and that we're mitigating; offering (where applicable) assistance switching to fallback region. draft: "We're experiencing transient serving degradation in EU, team is mitigating; no data loss; optional migration to eu-central available."

cs-tom: sent to two affected customers, one accepted trial redirect to eu-central. ops-team to assist.

oncall-alex: next steps: 1) hold autoscaler config stable for 30m, 2) slowly uncordon nodes after kernel/driver verified, 3) watch for crashloop recurrence, 4) run synthetic smoke tests for tail latency. who can run smoke?

runtime-jon: I'll run smoke and instrumented perf sweep (small tokens, long-context cases) and post results.

sre-maya: monitoring: setting alert suppression for repeated identical pages (to avoid noise) and enabling detailed pod restart tracing for this thread. created a temporary incident tag `incident:3478901234` on logs.

infra-li: rollback of AMI completed for green node set, replacing 6 nodes; draining and replacing the ones with kernel oops. progress: 4/6 replaced, 2 left draining.

incident-bot: update: auto-page suppressed for repeated restarts; incident severity remains P1; timeline note created.

eng-prod: quick note - consider adding preflight driver validation to node bootstrap to fail early (detect nvml mismatch) before node joins cluster. will draft RFC.

support-sarah: CS updated customers. one customer noted that queued fallback impacted UX; offered credit and engineering support.

cs-tom: customer acceptance for temporary region redirect confirmed; coordinating cutover.

noncall-alex: observed decrease in 5xxs from 30% -> 2% after rollback/provisioning stable nodes. still watching for residual tail errors.

runtime-jon: smoke: all tests green, latency tail stable. logs show no more `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED`.

sre-maya: setting postmortem owners: eng-prod (root cause AMI/driver rollout process), infra-li (autoscaler template rollback process), runtime-jon (runtime hardening), support-sarah & cs-tom (customer comms). We should schedule a blameless postmortem.

noncall-alex: thanks all. closing handoff to post-incident review. if anything reoccurs, re-open thread or page oncall. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident closed (3478902099) - final note: primary cause - driver/AMI mismatch + aggressive autoscaler reaction creating rapid scale up/down -> node flaps -> crashloops/brownout. remediation: rollback AMI, stabilize autoscaler min/max, add driver preflight check.
